records.text: On 2023-05-20, the user asked how fishing boats cope with waves and rough seas during deep-sea fishing expeditions. The assistant explained that such boats are generally larger, heavier, and built from durable materials; ballast systems help stabilize them; specialized stronger fishing lines and nets withstand turbulent conditions; radar and GPS support navigation and fish location; reliable communications connect crews with shore and other boats; and experienced crews are important for handling hazards.

On 2023-05-20, the user asked how fishing boats address crew motion sickness in rough seas. The assistant suggested motion-sickness medicines such as Dramamine or scopolamine, ginger, fresh air on deck, hydration while avoiding alcohol and caffeine, light and plain food while avoiding spicy or greasy food, rest and sleep, and acupressure wristbands.

On 2023-05-20, the user asked what happens if a crew member becomes severely seasick during a deep-sea fishing expedition and whether medical professionals are aboard. The assistant said fishing boats usually do not carry medical professionals, but generally have first-aid kits and emergency supplies. The captain or a crew member with relevant training or experience may provide care; for a critical condition, the boat may return to shore for hospital treatment or contact the coast guard or other emergency medical services. The assistant also recommended prevention, including motion-sickness medication, hydration, light meals, rest, and crew training in first aid and emergency procedures.
records.topic: Severe seasickness and onboard medical response
